title: Coda: Two Landscapes
voice: Unsigned gallery voice; curation/voice/style-guide.md as amended 2026-10-16 (Feeling and message)
dateBasis: UTC, from the archived creation timestamp
method: Depth pass, October 16, 2026. Both works were inspected again from the published WebP at 1200 px. Dates and stroke counts come from data/gallery.json; the March 15, 2023 purchase and transfers from curation/research/onchain/collector-acquisitions.json; the March 2023 burns from curation/research/onchain/README.md. scope: The owned subset: the 2 works the locked structure places in this room, in room order.
introduction: Two landscapes to end the wing. They were painted on March 15, 2023, in the two hours after the collection piece, and they are the last Rawblocks works. There is no head in either one. A sun sets through a stand of trees, and light falls through a forest onto a floor of fallen trunks. The artist had just finished a square with every creature of the series crowded into it, and then painted trees, twice, with more strokes than either of the series' origin pieces.

They hang here as a coda, apart from the rooms, because they look like nothing else in the series. The brushwork is the series' brushwork, soft discs of color with scribble and line over them, turned for once on trees and sky. That same evening the collector bought the collection piece and the series went to him, and in the days after, the unsold copies of the year's inks went to the burn address by the hundred. The last two things the artist painted before the fire were a sunset and a forest with the light coming through.

chapters.title: Two Landscapes
chapters.opening: Both painted on March 15, 2023, the sunset first and the forest half an hour later, in the two hours after the collection piece.

works.title: nnxyz rawblocks #64
works.text: A sunset through trees. A yellow sun blazes at the top with rays of pink, blue and yellow, and under it a stand of red-trunked trees with green crowns stands on a field of gold and orange, ruled with dark lines like a floor. The whole picture is painted in soft discs with scribble over them, and the sun's rays reach every corner. With 831 recorded strokes it is one of the two most worked drawings in the series. Ninety minutes after packing every creature of the year into the collection piece, the artist painted a sun with no face and trees with no one under them. In August the artist had written of a journey into the sun. This is the sun, reached, and it does not grin.
works.caption: A yellow sun blazes through a stand of red-trunked trees with green crowns, over a field of gold.
works.reading: The rays are drawn as long soft strokes from the sun at the upper center, in yellow, pink and blue. The trees are a row of thin red trunks with green and yellow scribble for leaves. The field below is painted in gold with dark ruled lines and blue scribble.

works.title: nnxyz rawblocks #65
works.text: Light through a forest. Tall dark trees stand at the sides and a beam of pale light falls between them onto a clearing, where fallen trunks lie in the foreground painted in brown and red. Soft discs of white and lilac float in the light. Half an hour after the sunset, the light has moved from the sky to the ground, and the picture is dark except where it falls. With 1,061 recorded strokes it is the most worked drawing in the Rawblocks, and the last. The beam is the searchlight of the whole collection, the one that lit the eyes in May and crossed the skulls in September, and here it falls on fallen trees in an empty wood. Nobody is in the picture. That is the last thing the series has to say, and it took more strokes than anything before it.
works.caption: Pale light falls through tall dark trees onto a clearing where fallen trunks lie in the foreground.
works.reading: The beam is a broad diagonal of pale grey from the upper left to the center. The trees are drawn in black and green scribble with white highlights. The fallen trunks are painted in brown and red with white line, lying at angles across the bottom.

closing: The sun in the first picture is the sun-face of the series without its face. Look at it once more, then at the forest, where the light falls on nothing but trees. That is where the Rawblocks end: with the mask set down, the crowd handed over, and the artist looking at the light.
